scope: Exact-unit engineering evidence for two designated bench switches on an Intel Home Assistant testbed

provenance.basis: Operator-transcribed native API observations, Home Assistant state and protected testbed evidence; not a retained raw RF capture.
provenance.limitations: Full native snapshots from earlier pairing attempts were not separately retained before subsequent sessions replaced them; the operator record preserves their observed results.

pairing_attempts.note: Supported candidate observed; precise arrival time is unknown.

confirmation_basis: The deployed code requires positive admission transmission completion plus a fresh matching report received after admission transmission began; the report can be buffered before completion. No raw transmission capture is claimed.

control_preparation.enablement: After clean stop and network identity checks, temporarily set the wrapper options to the exact existing saved gateway identity and experimental_phase; retained image, firmware, journal, paired registry and paths.
control_preparation.daemon_after_enable: ready, controls enabled, MCU heartbeat and MCU query mode
control_preparation.home_assistant: The physical integration remained disconnected with a stale snapshot. One reviewed physical-entry reload led to setup_retry; independent authenticated GETs and the installed client info/snapshot validators in fresh processes succeeded. The original HA in-process session was not exercised by those probes.
control_preparation.refresh: One explicit HA refresh returned unknown without a surfaced request ID; no corresponding daemon ledger record was observed. This does not prove the request was never sent.

restoration.options: Original options restored byte-for-byte, including disabled mode and original blank network seeds.
restoration.daemon: ready, controls disabled, host heartbeat and raw query mode
restoration.identity_and_registry: same persisted network and two paired peers; current journal and database retained
restoration.home_assistant_entities: Immediately after disabled-mode restoration, three original physical output entity IDs remained present and unavailable while the integration was in setup_retry; subsequent recovery is documented separately.
restoration.diagnosis: One automatic setup retry recorded aiodns DNS error code 1 (answer with no data), surfaced as ClientConnectorDNSError then LivoloError during in-process info(). Fresh-process validation succeeded; the cause of the resolver difference is unproven. Temporary scoped debug logging was restored.

production_environment: Production Home Assistant and other radios unchanged.

recovery.action: One graceful restart of the existing Intel test Home Assistant container after the DNS failure was recorded. The physical daemon and radio were not restarted.
recovery.home_assistant: Same container identity, image, mounts, networks, two existing Livolo entries and endpoint configuration retained. Both physical and simulator entries loaded and reported connected via their event streams.
recovery.physical_daemon: Same daemon process and image; ready, nonsimulated, controls disabled, two registered peers.
recovery.entities_and_ledger: All 20 prior Livolo entity registry records, including the three physical output IDs, were unchanged; comparison found the same six physical daemon command records.
recovery.limitations: Recovery after restart does not establish the mechanism behind the resolver divergence. No pairing, state-refresh replay, or output command was issued as part of recovery.
